Other frameworks: class names, helpers from `"@danitesler/ayywi"`, and `import "@danitesler/ayywi/elements"` for `<ayy-toolbar>`, `<ayy-action-bar>`, `<ayy-menu>`, `<ayy-command>`, `<ayy-navbar>`, `<ayy-app-shell>`, `<ayy-toc>`, `<ayy-inline-edit>`, `<ayy-combobox>`, `<ayy-tag-input>`, `<ayy-record-picker>`, `<ayy-date-picker>`, `<ayy-date-range>`, `<ayy-time-picker>`, `<ayy-date-time-picker>`, `<ayy-color-picker>`, `<ayy-shortcut-recorder>`, `<ayy-tabs>`, `<ayy-carousel>`, `<ayy-dialog>`, `<ayy-popover>`, `<ayy-tooltip>`, `<ayy-swipe>`, `<ayy-table>`, `<ayy-grid>`.

## Button (Actions)
Triggers an action. Pill-shaped, monochrome primary with a subtle lift on hover.
- Classes: `.ayy-button` `.ayy-button--secondary` `.ayy-button--outline` `.ayy-button--ghost` `.ayy-button--destructive` `.ayy-button--link` `.ayy-button--ring` `.ayy-button--sm` `.ayy-button--lg` `.ayy-button--icon` `.ayy-button--icon-sm` `.ayy-button--icon-lg` `.ayy-button--block` `.ayy-button--start` `.ayy-button--end`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, loading
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg` `icon` `icon-sm` `icon-lg`
- JS: buttonClass({ variant?, size?, block?, align?, className? }) → string. Loading in HTML: aria-busy="true" plus <span class="ayy-spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span> as the first child.
- A11y: Icon-only buttons need aria-label and should always have a visible Tooltip on hover/focus. Use disabled on <button>; on <a> use aria-disabled="true" (the class handles both). Visible focus ring on :focus-visible is built in — never remove it. While it works, set aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: loading). Don't disable it: focus would jump away.

## Hover actions (Actions)
Icon buttons that float over a picture, a video frame or a card — a capture's Copy, Annotate, Pin and ⋯. Each button has its own frosted background so it reads over any image, or the buttons share one glass bar (group). Reveal keeps them out of the way until the picture is hovered or focused; every button names itself in a tooltip.
- Classes: `.ayy-hover-actions` `.ayy-hover-actions--top-start` `.ayy-hover-actions--top-end` `.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-start` `.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-end` `.ayy-hover-actions--group` `.ayy-hover-actions--reveal` `.ayy-hover-action`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, revealed
- JS: hoverActionsClass({ position?, group?, reveal?, className? }) → string; hoverActionClass({ className? }) → string
- A11y: Every button needs an aria-label (React's label sets it); the icon is decorative. Revealed rows are still in the tab order: focusing a button shows the row, so keyboard users reach every action. Touch screens have no hover, so --reveal rows always show there; never hide the only way to do something behind hover.

## Toolbar (Actions)
A row or column of tools and actions for one surface: an editor's tools, a canvas rail, formatting over a selection. role="toolbar" makes it one Tab stop with arrow keys between items; tools that stay on are aria-pressed. Square icon buttons (or icon and label), groups, separators and a spacer; plain, vertical, floating or scrolling.
- Classes: `.ayy-toolbar` `.ayy-toolbar--vertical` `.ayy-toolbar--floating` `.ayy-toolbar--scroll` `.ayy-toolbar--sm` `.ayy-toolbar__group` `.ayy-toolbar__separator` `.ayy-toolbar__spacer` `.ayy-toolbar__button`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md`
- Element: `<ayy-toolbar>`, events `ayy-press`
- JS: toolbarClass({ vertical?, floating?, scroll?, size?, className? }) → string; toolbarButtonClass, toolbarGroupClass, toolbarSeparatorClass, toolbarSpacerClass constants; connectToolbar(el) → { refresh, destroy } wires the keyboard pattern on plain markup.
- A11y: role="toolbar" with an aria-label. Tab reaches it once (the last tool used, else the pressed one, else the first); Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between tools, mirrored in RTL; Home/End jump to the ends. Disabled tools are skipped. Every icon-only tool needs an aria-label ("Rectangle"), and the name shouldn't change with its state — aria-pressed says whether it's on. Text fields and radio groups (swatches, a segmented control) inside keep their own arrow keys; the radio group is one stop. On is a wash tile with a hairline, not colour alone; High Contrast fills it with the system highlight.

## Action bar (Actions)
Floating bottom multi-select bar that animates into view when one or more rows or cards are selected in a Table, Grid or List. Shows the selected count, a clear button (Esc), and bulk actions such as Edit, Duplicate, Copy, Archive and Delete.
- Classes: `.ayy-action-bar` `.ayy-action-bar--fixed` `.ayy-action-bar__selection` `.ayy-action-bar__count` `.ayy-action-bar__close` `.ayy-action-bar__separator` `.ayy-action-bar__actions` `.ayy-action-bar__button` `.ayy-action-bar__button--primary` `.ayy-action-bar__button--secondary` `.ayy-action-bar__button--destructive` `.ayy-action-bar__button--icon`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, open
- Element: `<ayy-action-bar>`, events `ayy-clear`
- JS: actionBarClass({ fixed?, className? }) → string; actionBarButtonClass({ variant?, primary?, secondary?, destructive?, icon?, className? }) → string; actionBarSelectionClass, actionBarCountClass, actionBarCloseClass, actionBarSeparatorClass, actionBarActionsClass constants; connectActionBar(bar, { onClear? }) → { refresh, syncCount, destroy } wires keyboard navigation, Escape/close clearing, and count updates.
- A11y: role="toolbar" with an aria-label ("Bulk actions"): one Tab stop, Left/Right arrow keys (mirrored in RTL) and Home/End move between the clear button and actions. Pressing Escape or clicking ActionBarClose clears the selection and dismisses the bar. Icon-only buttons inside the bar must have an aria-label (e.g. aria-label="Delete selected") and always be wrapped in a Tooltip. High Contrast mode borders the bar in CanvasText and highlights primary or open buttons with Highlight.

## Dropdown menu (Actions)

- A11y: Opening moves focus to the first item; arrows move, Home/End jump, letters jump to matching items. ArrowRight / ArrowLeft open and close submenus (mirrored in RTL); Esc inside a submenu closes only that panel. Esc or Tab closes the menu and focus returns to the trigger. Icon-only triggers (⋯) need aria-label.

## Command palette (Actions)
A search field over a grouped list of actions and places: type to filter, arrows to move, Enter to run. Inline in a page or popover, or as a dialog near the top of the screen opened with ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Items can show an icon, a shortcut and a count.
- Classes: `.ayy-command` `.ayy-command__search` `.ayy-command__input` `.ayy-command__list` `.ayy-command__group` `.ayy-command__label` `.ayy-command__item` `.ayy-command__content` `.ayy-command__title` `.ayy-command__description` `.ayy-command__meta` `.ayy-command__empty` `.ayy-command__footer`
- States: focus, disabled, selected, empty, filtered
- Element: `<ayy-command shortcut manual>`, events `ayy-select`
- JS: connectCommand(root, { onSelect?, filter?, reorder? }) → { refresh(activateFirst?), reset, destroy } wires filtering, the arrows, Enter and the pointer on plain markup; Enter clicks the highlighted item. Better matches move up (reorder: false when a framework owns the items; React Command ranks its children itself). commandMatches(text, query) is the matching rule (every typed word starts a word, or one word anywhere); commandItemText(item); commandItemDetails(item); commandScore(title, description, keywords, query). commandClass, commandInputClass, commandListClass, commandItemClass, commandSearchIcon (SVG markup).
- A11y: The WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox that is always shown: focus stays in the input, aria-activedescendant names the highlighted item, and the first match is highlighted as you type. Up/Down move (wrapping), PageUp/PageDown move five, Enter runs the highlighted item, Esc clears the field and a second Esc closes the dialog. Groups are role="group" named by their heading, so screen readers say "Go to" when the highlight enters one. Shortcuts in items are read as words ("Command N"); icons are hidden. The dialog palette is a modal <dialog> named by aria-label; focus goes to the input when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes.

## Floating action button (Actions)
The one main action of a phone screen (New task, Compose, Scan), as a round button floating at the bottom inline-end corner over the content. Extended adds a label. Fixed to the viewport and clear of the home indicator; as a direct child of an App shell it sits in the shell's corner and above its bottom nav on phones.
- Classes: `.ayy-fab` `.ayy-fab--extended` `.ayy-fab--secondary` `.ayy-fab--sm` `.ayy-fab--inline`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled
- Sizes: `sm` `md`
- JS: fabClass({ variant?, size?, extended?, inline?, className? }) → string; fabVariants, fabSizes.
- A11y: An icon-only FAB needs an aria-label that says the action ("New task"), not the icon ("Plus"). Put it after the main content in the DOM so it comes after what it acts on in the tab order, not before the page. It must not cover content for good: the App shell keeps it out of the bottom nav, and lists need room at their end (padding-block-end of the FAB's height) so the last row can scroll clear of it.

## Navbar (Navigation)
Sticky site header on translucent glass: brand at the start, links and actions at the end, content centred at page width. On phones a menu button folds the links into a panel under the bar.
- Classes: `.ayy-navbar` `.ayy-navbar__inner` `.ayy-navbar__brand` `.ayy-navbar__nav` `.ayy-navbar__link` `.ayy-navbar__actions` `.ayy-navbar__toggle`
- States: hover, focus, selected, open
- Element: `<ayy-navbar>`
- JS: navbarClass, navbarInnerClass, navbarBrandClass, navbarNavClass, navbarLinkClass, navbarActionsClass, navbarToggleClass constants; connectNavbar(header) wires the phone menu and returns a cleanup; navbarMenuIcon (the Hugeicons menu icon as SVG markup).
- A11y: Use <header> for the bar and <nav aria-label="Main"> for the links; one main nav per page. Mark the current page with aria-current="page", not only with colour. Put a .ayy-skip-link before the navbar so keyboard users can jump past it. The menu button is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the nav (set for you). Focus stays on it when the panel opens; Tab moves into the links, Esc closes the panel and returns focus to the button. The closed panel is display: none, so its links are out of the tab order until it opens.

## App shell (Navigation)
The frame of a web app: a sidebar beside a main area, each scrolling on its own. On phones the sidebar becomes a Bottom nav (recommended), a drawer or a sideways row. Settings reuse it inside a full-size Dialog.
- Classes: `.ayy-app-shell` `.ayy-app-shell__sidebar` `.ayy-app-shell__brand` `.ayy-app-shell__logotype` `.ayy-app-shell__nav` `.ayy-app-shell__link` `.ayy-app-shell__group` `.ayy-app-shell__group-label` `.ayy-app-shell__group--collapsible` `.ayy-app-shell__link--action` `.ayy-app-shell__list` `.ayy-app-shell__sublist` `.ayy-app-shell__collapse` `.ayy-app-shell__link--sub` `.ayy-app-shell__footer` `.ayy-app-shell__main` `.ayy-app-shell__bar` `.ayy-app-shell--settings` `.ayy-app-shell__back` `.ayy-app-shell__head` `.ayy-app-shell__title` `.ayy-app-shell__toggle` `.ayy-app-shell--collapsed` `.ayy-app-shell--hover-preview` `.ayy-app-shell--drawer` `.ayy-app-shell__detail` `.ayy-app-shell__resize` `.ayy-app-shell__resize--detail` `.ayy-app-shell--resizing` `.ayy-app-shell--md` `.ayy-app-shell--sm`
- States: hover, focus, selected, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- Element: `<ayy-app-shell size collapsed hover-preview>`, events `ayy-collapse-change`, `ayy-resize`
- JS: appShellClass, appShellSidebarClass, appShellBrandClass, appShellNavClass, appShellLinkClass, appShellFooterClass, appShellMainClass, appShellGroupClass, appShellGroupLabelClass, appShellGroupCollapsibleClass, appShellListClass, appShellSublistClass, appShellCollapseClass, appShellLinkSubClass, appShellBarClass, appShellToggleClass, appShellCollapsedClass, appShellHoverPreviewClass, appShellSmClass, appShellMdClass, appShellDrawerClass, appShellDetailClass, appShellResizeClass, appShellResizeDetailClass, appShellResizingClass, appShellSizes constants; appShellSettingsClass, appShellBackClass, appShellTitleClass, appShellHeadClass, appShellLogotypeClass constants; connectAppShell(shell, options) wires the phone drawer, desktop sidebar collapse and hover preview, and Esc in settings, and returns a cleanup; appShellMenuIcon (the Hugeicons menu icon as SVG markup); appShellBackIcon (the settings back arrow, mirrored in RTL).
- A11y: The sidebar is an <aside> (a complementary landmark) and the content is a <main>: one <main> per page, and no other element with that landmark. Keep one <nav aria-label="Main"> in the sidebar. The bottom nav repeats its top destinations and only one of the two shows at a time, so it can use the same label. Give any other nav (a settings menu) its own label. Mark the current page with aria-current="page" in both the sidebar and the bottom nav. The link also gets a tint and a heavier weight, so colour is not the only cue; High Contrast mode fills it with the system highlight. Put a .ayy-skip-link before the shell, pointing at an id on <main>, so keyboard users can jump past the sidebar. Group with a heading and a list: the <p> label names the <ul> through aria-labelledby, so a screen reader announces "Workspace, list, 3 items". A collapse is a native <details>: Enter and Space toggle it, and the open state is exposed for you. Don't add aria-expanded to the <summary>. Mark the current child with aria-current="page" and open its collapse. A closed collapse that holds the current page is drawn bolder, so the location isn't hidden. Both columns are scroll containers. If a column can scroll but holds nothing focusable, give it tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it. The drawer's toggle is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the sidebar (set for you). Opening moves focus to the first link in the drawer and makes the rest of the shell inert; Esc closes it and returns focus to the toggle. Settings mode: name the dialog by the sidebar title (aria-labelledby on the <dialog>), give the sections' nav its own label ("Settings"), mark the open section with aria-current="page", and make the section's Top bar title its <h1> (the sidebar title is an <h2>). Render the main as a <div> so the page keeps one <main>. On phones, opening a section moves focus to the main, and its back button returns it to the section's link. A collapsed sidebar with hover preview opens when keyboard focus moves into it (:focus-visible), so every link is reachable and readable from the keyboard; links without an icon are only in the tab order while it's open. Give rail links a title for a tooltip with the pointer. In a dialog, Esc closes settings and focus returns to what opened them. A settings shell on a page of its own leaves through its __back on Esc, except when focus is in a text field or an open menu, popover or dialog has it. A resize handle is a separator you can focus: arrow keys move the edge by 16px (Shift 64), Home and End jump to the limits, and aria-valuenow / min / max are kept in px. The detail pane is an <aside>: label it (aria-label) for what it shows, and move focus into it when you open it from the main area. The phone sidebar (closed drawer) is visibility: hidden, and the bottom nav is display: none from 48rem, so hidden links are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.

## Bottom nav (Navigation)
A phone app's tab bar: top-level destinations, each an icon over a short label, pinned to the bottom of the screen within thumb reach and clear of the home indicator. Supports three sizes and compact mode for more items. Inside an App shell it replaces the sidebar on phones.
- Classes: `.ayy-bottom-nav` `.ayy-bottom-nav--sm` `.ayy-bottom-nav--md` `.ayy-bottom-nav--lg` `.ayy-bottom-nav--compact` `.ayy-bottom-nav--icon-only` `.ayy-bottom-nav__link` `.ayy-bottom-nav__label`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: bottomNavClass({ size?, compact?, iconOnly?, className? }) → string; bottomNavSizes constant; bottomNavLinkClass, bottomNavLabelClass constants.
- A11y: It's a <nav>: give it an aria-label ("Main" by default in React). Inside an App shell only one of it and the sidebar shows at a time, so they can share the label. Mark the current page with aria-current="page". It also gets a pill and a heavier weight, so colour isn't the only cue; High Contrast mode fills the pill with the system highlight. Visible labels are recommended. When iconOnly is used, screen reader text is preserved via visually hidden labels. A "More" tab is a <button> with aria-expanded (set for you when it's an app shell toggle), not a link to "#". Each tab is at least the control height of its size tier (sm 28px, md 32px, lg 40px), maintaining comfortable touch targets. Outside an App shell, content above it needs bottom padding (or to end before it) so the last line isn't hidden behind the bar.

## Top bar (Navigation)
A phone screen's header: a back button, the screen's title (and a subtitle), and one to three actions, sticky at the top and clear of the notch. Centred title for iOS-style screens, a large title on its own line for a tab's first screen, and an optional second row for a search bar or a segmented control.
- Classes: `.ayy-top-bar` `.ayy-top-bar--center` `.ayy-top-bar--large` `.ayy-top-bar__back` `.ayy-top-bar__title` `.ayy-top-bar__heading` `.ayy-top-bar__subtitle` `.ayy-top-bar__actions` `.ayy-top-bar__row`
- States: hover, focus
- JS: topBarClass({ center?, large?, className? }) → string; topBarBackClass, topBarTitleClass, topBarHeadingClass, topBarSubtitleClass, topBarActionsClass, topBarRowClass constants; topBarBackIcon (the back chevron's SVG markup, mirrored in RTL).
- A11y: The title is the page's <h1>, so a screen reader user knows where they landed after navigating. A chevron-only back button is named "Back" (translate it); with a visible name ("Lists") the text names it. Icon buttons in __actions each need an aria-label. Keep to three; put the rest in a Menu behind a More button. The chevron is directional, so it points right in RTL, where "back" is.

## Footer (Navigation)
The site footer at the end of every website page: brand and a line about the product, columns of links, and a bottom row for copyright and legal links. Centred at page width like the navbar.
- Classes: `.ayy-footer` `.ayy-footer__inner` `.ayy-footer__brand` `.ayy-footer__nav` `.ayy-footer__group` `.ayy-footer__heading` `.ayy-footer__list` `.ayy-footer__link` `.ayy-footer__bottom`
- States: hover, focus
- JS: footerClass, footerInnerClass, footerBrandClass, footerNavClass, footerGroupClass, footerHeadingClass, footerListClass, footerLinkClass, footerBottomClass constants.
- A11y: Use <footer> once per page, outside <main>: it's the contentinfo landmark. The link columns are a <nav aria-label="Footer">, distinct from the navbar's "Main". Each column's heading names its list, so screen readers announce "Product, list, 4 items".

## Breadcrumb (Navigation)
Trail from the top level down to the current page (Home / Case studies / Oktopost). Plain, or a blurred pill for heroes.
- Classes: `.ayy-breadcrumb` `.ayy-breadcrumb--pill` `.ayy-breadcrumb__list` `.ayy-breadcrumb__item` `.ayy-breadcrumb__link`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- JS: breadcrumbClass({ pill?, className? }) → string; breadcrumbListClass, breadcrumbItemClass, breadcrumbLinkClass constants.
- A11y: Wrap it in <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> and use an <ol>, so it's announced as an ordered path. The current page is plain text with aria-current="page", not a link to itself.

## Pagination (Navigation)
Previous, page numbers with gaps, and next, for a long table or list. On phones only previous, the current page and next stay.
- Classes: `.ayy-pagination` `.ayy-pagination__link` `.ayy-pagination__link--step` `.ayy-pagination__ellipsis`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected
- JS: paginationClass, paginationEllipsisClass constants; paginationLinkClass({ step?, className? }) → string; paginationRange(page, count, siblings = 1) → (number | "…")[] — which pages to show, always the same number of slots.
- A11y: It's a <nav aria-label="Pagination">: give a second one on the page a different label. The current page has aria-current="page"; it's outlined and bolder as well as tinted. Previous and next say so in words; their arrows are decorative and mirror in right-to-left text. An end you can't go past is aria-disabled (or disabled): screen readers hear it's unavailable. After a page change in place, move focus to the top of the updated table or list, or announce the new range.

## Steps (Navigation)
Where you are in a short flow (sign-up, checkout, import): numbered steps with the current one filled, the done ones ticked and the rest waiting. Pure CSS: aria-current="step" is the only state.
- Classes: `.ayy-steps` `.ayy-steps--vertical` `.ayy-steps__item` `.ayy-steps__label`
- States: selected
- JS: stepsClass({ vertical?, className? }) → string; stepsItemClass, stepsLabelClass constants.
- A11y: It's an ordered list with aria-current="step" on the current item, so screen readers hear "step 2 of 4, current". Give the <ol> an aria-label ("Checkout progress"). Done steps say so in text, not only with a tick: put an .ayy-sr-only "Done: " before their label (React does it). The markers are generated content with empty alt text, so numbers aren't read twice.

## Table of contents (Navigation)
On-page table of contents with a scrollspy: a rail of section links where the one you're reading gets an accent bar. Optional numbers, one level of nesting, sticky beside long content.
- Classes: `.ayy-toc` `.ayy-toc--sticky` `.ayy-toc__title` `.ayy-toc__bar` `.ayy-toc__toggle` `.ayy-toc__toggle-icon` `.ayy-toc__toggle-current` `.ayy-toc__toggle-caret` `.ayy-toc__list` `.ayy-toc__link` `.ayy-toc__number`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- Element: `<ayy-toc offset>`, events `ayy-value-change`
- JS: tocClass({ sticky?, className? }) → string; tocTitleClass, tocListClass, tocLinkClass, tocNumberClass, tocBarClass, tocToggleClass, tocToggleIconClass, tocToggleCurrentClass, tocToggleCaretClass constants; tocMenuIcon, tocChevronIcon SVG strings; connectToc(root, { offset?, onChange? }) → cleanup — the scrollspy and mobile menu.
- A11y: It's a <nav> with a name (the title via aria-labelledby, or aria-label="On this page"), so it shows up in landmark lists. The current section is aria-current="location", announced by screen readers, not only drawn as a colour bar. Links are ordinary in-page anchors: they work without JS, and the navbar's scroll-padding keeps targets clear of the sticky header. Links grow to a 40px target at touch density. On phones the visible title is hidden but still names the nav, and the sticky toggle pill is labeled via aria-label.

A rounded search field with a magnifier and a clear button, and optionally a Cancel button after it, as at the top of a phone list. A <form role="search"> around an <input type="search">, so phones show a Search key. The clear button only shows while there's text.

- Element: `<ayy-shortcut-recorder value label bare>`, events `ayy-change`, `ayy-recording`
- JS: Shortcuts are strings like "Mod+Shift+K" (Mod = ⌘ on Apple devices, Ctrl elsewhere; also Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Meta). shortcutFromEvent(event, { bare? }) → the shortcut a keydown makes, or null for modifiers alone; matchShortcut(event, "Mod+K") → boolean, for your own handlers, by physical key, so it works on any layout (Russian Cmd+У is Mod+E); shortcutKeys(s, platform?) → ["⌘", "K"] (Super on Linux, Win on Windows); shortcutLabel(s, platform?) → "Command K"; shortcutHtml(s, platform?) → markup; syncShortcuts(root?, platform?) redraws static .ayy-shortcut[data-keys] for Apple and Linux devices (@danitesler/ayywi/elements does it on load); getPlatform(); isApplePlatform(); isWindowsPlatform(); isLinuxPlatform(); keyFromCode(code). connectShortcutRecorder(button, { value?, label?, bare?, onChange?, onRecordingChange? }) → { setValue, destroy }. shortcutClass, shortcutRecorderClass({ className? }).
- A11y: Keycaps are aria-hidden and a visually hidden label says the keys in words ("Command Shift K"), so screen readers don't read "place of interest sign". The recorder is a toggle button: aria-pressed="true" while listening, and its aria-label says the action, the keys and how to cancel ("Capture area: Press keys, or Escape to cancel"). While it listens it takes every key, Tab included (Tab cancels and moves on), so it can never trap focus. Pause the app's own shortcuts while recording (onRecordingChange / ayy-recording), or pressing one would run it. A clash is shown with aria-invalid on the recorder and a hint saying which action already uses it; the border is not the only cue.

## Settings (Forms)
Preferences as rows: a label and a one-line hint at the start, the control (Switch, Select, Shortcut recorder, Button) at the end, grouped under a heading in a card with hairlines between rows. A row can also be a link to a sub-page with the current value and a chevron, or an action like Sign out, as phone settings are.
- Classes: `.ayy-settings` `.ayy-settings--plain` `.ayy-settings__title` `.ayy-settings__description` `.ayy-settings__list` `.ayy-settings__row` `.ayy-settings__row--stack` `.ayy-settings__text` `.ayy-settings__label` `.ayy-settings__hint` `.ayy-settings__control` `.ayy-settings__link` `.ayy-settings__value` `.ayy-settings__link--destructive`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, error, destructive
- JS: settingsClass({ plain?, className? }), settingsRowClass({ stack?, link?, destructive?, className? }) → class strings; settingsChevronIcon (SVG markup for a link row's chevron, mirrored in RTL).
- A11y: Each group is a <section> labelled by its <h2>, so screen-reader users can jump between groups. Every control needs a name: give SettingsRow htmlFor and the control that id, so the label is a real <label for>. For a Switch, put the id on the switch's input. Point the control's aria-describedby at the hint (`${htmlFor}-hint`) so the explanation is read with it. A link row is one <a> or <button>: its whole text, value included, is its name. Use <a href> when it opens a page, <button> when it does something. Controls wrap under the label on narrow screens instead of shrinking below a usable size.

## Page header (Layout)
The top of an app screen: an optional breadcrumb or eyebrow, the page title (the h1), one line of description, and the page's actions at the end — below the title on phones.
- Classes: `.ayy-page-header` `.ayy-page-header__title` `.ayy-page-header__description` `.ayy-page-header__actions`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: pageHeaderClass, pageHeaderTitleClass, pageHeaderDescriptionClass, pageHeaderActionsClass constants.
- A11y: The title is the page's only <h1>; sections below it start at <h2>. Keep the actions after the title in the source, so screen readers hear what the page is before what it can do. A breadcrumb above the title is its own <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">.

## Showcase (Layout)
An interactive container for previewing UI across viewports (desktop, tablet, mobile), with a toolbar for device switching, custom controls, and code snippets.
- Classes: `.ayy-showcase` `.ayy-showcase__header` `.ayy-showcase__title` `.ayy-showcase__actions` `.ayy-showcase__stage` `.ayy-showcase__viewport` `.ayy-showcase__viewport--desktop` `.ayy-showcase__viewport--tablet` `.ayy-showcase__viewport--mobile` `.ayy-showcase__body`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: showcaseClass, showcaseHeaderClass, showcaseTitleClass, showcaseActionsClass, showcaseStageClass, showcaseBodyClass, showcaseDevices constants; showcaseViewportClass({ device?, className? }) → string.
- A11y: Give the Showcase an aria-labelledby pointing to its ShowcaseTitle. Device switchers must have accessible labels describing the active viewport.

## Card (Layout)
Surface that groups related content. Flat at rest with an inset top highlight; optional lift and pointer-following spotlight. The view type (view) is a capture, recording or picture to open: the picture letterboxed over a blurred copy of itself, a recording's length in the corner, and its title, details, badges and Hover actions revealed on hover.
- Classes: `.ayy-card` `.ayy-card--interactive` `.ayy-card--spotlight` `.ayy-card--featured` `.ayy-card__header` `.ayy-card__title` `.ayy-card__description` `.ayy-card__content` `.ayy-card__footer` `.ayy-card__media` `.ayy-card__link` `.ayy-card--view` `.ayy-card__view-media` `.ayy-card__view-backdrop` `.ayy-card__view-image` `.ayy-card__view-badge` `.ayy-card__view-play` `.ayy-card__view-body` `.ayy-card__view-text` `.ayy-card__view-title` `.ayy-card__view-meta` `.ayy-card__view-badges`
- States: hover, focus, selected, menu-open
- JS: cardClass({ interactive?, spotlight?, featured?, view?, className? }) → string; cardHeaderClass, cardTitleClass, cardDescriptionClass, cardContentClass, cardFooterClass, cardMediaClass, cardLinkClass constants; trackSpotlight(pointerEvent) sets --ayy-mx/--ayy-my.
- A11y: If the whole card is a link, put ayy-card__link on the title's <a> — don't wrap the card in <a>. Screen readers then announce just the title, not the whole card. Media images are content: give them alt text, or alt="" when the title already says it all. Spotlight layers are pseudo-elements, invisible to assistive tech. View cards: when the picture opens something, CardViewMedia is a <button> or <a> with an aria-label that names the item and the action ("Annotate the pricing page capture from 2 minutes ago"); the body is decoration on top of it. View cards reveal their body and actions on focus as well as hover, and always show them on touch screens, so nothing is hover-only. The backdrop is aria-hidden.

## Tabs (Layout)
Segmented pill tabs switching between panels of related content. Full WAI-ARIA tabs keyboard support.
- Classes: `.ayy-tabs` `.ayy-tabs__list` `.ayy-tabs__tab` `.ayy-tabs__panel` `.ayy-tabs__count`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected
- Element: `<ayy-tabs value>`, events `ayy-value-change`
- JS: tabsClass/tabsListClass/tabsTabClass/tabsPanelClass/tabsCountClass constants; nextTabIndex(key, current, count, rtl) for custom keyboard handling.
- A11y: Arrow keys move between tabs (flipped in RTL), Home/End jump to first/last. Activation follows focus. Only the selected tab is in the tab order (roving tabindex). Give the tablist an aria-label when there's no visible heading.

## Accordion (Layout)
Questions and answers, or sections people open one at a time: native <details> in a stack with hairlines between them. Same name attribute on each and opening one closes the others.
- Classes: `.ayy-accordion` `.ayy-accordion__item` `.ayy-accordion__trigger` `.ayy-accordion__content`
- States: hover, focus, open
- JS: accordionClass, accordionItemClass, accordionTriggerClass, accordionContentClass constants.
- A11y: It's native <details>/<summary>: Enter and Space toggle it and the open state is announced. Don't add aria-expanded or a click handler. Keep the summary text short and complete (a question), since it's the only part people see. Find-in-page opens a closed item that contains the match.

## Carousel (Layout)
A strip of slides that scrolls sideways and snaps, with previous/next buttons that disable at the ends. Native scrolling: swipe, trackpad and arrow keys work without JS.
- Classes: `.ayy-carousel` `.ayy-carousel__track` `.ayy-carousel__slide` `.ayy-carousel__controls`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled
- Element: `<ayy-carousel>`
- JS: carouselClass, carouselTrackClass, carouselSlideClass, carouselControlsClass constants; connectCarousel(root) → cleanup — wires the buttons, aria-disabled at the ends and slide labels.
- A11y: The root is a named region with aria-roledescription="carousel"; each slide is a group named "n of total" unless you name it. The track is focusable, so arrow keys scroll it; the buttons stay focusable at the ends (aria-disabled, not disabled) so focus isn't lost. Nothing moves on its own, and smooth scrolling turns off under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Separator (Layout)
A hairline between blocks: full, fading out at both ends (between page sections), or vertical (between inline items).
- Classes: `.ayy-separator` `.ayy-separator--vertical` `.ayy-separator--fade`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: separatorClass({ orientation?, fade?, className? }) → string
- A11y: <hr> is a separator to screen readers. If the line is purely decorative, use role="presentation" or a CSS border instead. Vertical separators need aria-orientation="vertical" (the React component adds it).

## Dialog (Overlays)
Modal dialog built on the native <dialog> element: top layer, inert background, focus handling and Esc for free. Centred, or a side modal (drawer, sheet) that slides in from the inline-start or inline-end edge, or a bottom sheet for phones.
- Classes: `.ayy-dialog` `.ayy-dialog--sm` `.ayy-dialog--lg` `.ayy-dialog--xl` `.ayy-dialog--full` `.ayy-dialog--side-start` `.ayy-dialog--side-end` `.ayy-dialog--side-bottom` `.ayy-dialog__header` `.ayy-dialog__title` `.ayy-dialog__description` `.ayy-dialog__body` `.ayy-dialog__footer` `.ayy-dialog__close`
- States: hover, focus, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` `full`
- Element: `<ayy-dialog open persistent>`, events `ayy-open-change`
- JS: dialogClass({ size?, side?, className? }); isBackdropClick(dialog, event); dialogCloseIcon (the Hugeicons close icon as SVG markup). Without any JS helper: dialog.showModal() / dialog.close(), or natively <button commandfor="id" command="show-modal"> in modern browsers.
- A11y: Always include a DialogTitle (or aria-label on the dialog). Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to the trigger on close (native behaviour). Esc closes; background is inert while open; page scroll is locked. A side modal is still a modal: same rules. A body with only text that scrolls needs tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it; form fields inside make that unnecessary. Opening and closing fade/scale (side modals slide); the closing animation is skipped in browsers without @starting-style and under reduced motion.

## Popover (Overlays)
Non-modal floating panel anchored to a button. Built on the native popover attribute: top layer, click-outside and Esc to close.
- Classes: `.ayy-popover`
- States: open
- Element: `<ayy-popover side align open>`, events `ayy-open-change`
- JS: popoverClass constant; connectPopover(trigger, content, { side?, align?, offset?, crossAxisOffset?, boundary?, onToggle? }) → { open, close, isOpen, update, destroy }
- A11y: Give the content an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at its heading). The trigger gets aria-expanded automatically; Esc and click-outside close it and focus returns to the trigger. It's not a focus trap — use Dialog when the user must finish something first.

## Tooltip (Overlays)
Short hint on hover or keyboard focus. Works with CSS alone; with React Tooltip or <ayy-tooltip> it moves to the top layer (never clipped) and flips at screen edges.
- Classes: `.ayy-tooltip` `.ayy-tooltip__content`
- States: hover, focus, dismissed
- Element: `<ayy-tooltip side>`
- JS: tooltipClass, tooltipContentClass constants; enhanceTooltip(host) moves the bubble to the top layer and adds Esc (returns cleanup).
- A11y: Trigger must be focusable so keyboard users see it too. aria-describedby links trigger → tooltip (React does it automatically). Esc dismisses (WCAG 1.4.13); the bubble stays open while hovered.

## Alert (Feedback)
Inline message box with optional icon, title, description and actions.
- Classes: `.ayy-alert` `.ayy-alert--info` `.ayy-alert--success` `.ayy-alert--warning` `.ayy-alert--destructive` `.ayy-alert__title` `.ayy-alert__description` `.ayy-alert__actions`
- States: error
- JS: alertClass({ variant?, className? }) → string; alertTitleClass, alertDescriptionClass, alertActionsClass constants
- A11y: Static alerts need no role. If it appears in response to an action, add role="alert" (urgent) or role="status" (polite). The icon is decorative: aria-hidden="true". The text must carry the meaning.

## Toast (Feedback)
Short, temporary notification. One framework-free toast() function renders into a shared region in the top layer (visible above dialogs). Supports text notifications, visual content previews (CardToast) for images, videos, and GIFs, and embedded in-place feedback (InlineToast).
- Classes: `.ayy-toaster` `.ayy-toaster__clear` `.ayy-toast` `.ayy-toast--success` `.ayy-toast--warning` `.ayy-toast--destructive` `.ayy-toast--info` `.ayy-toast--card` `.ayy-toast--card-split` `.ayy-toast--card-split--vertical` `.ayy-toast--long` `.ayy-toast--inline` `.ayy-toast--inline--success` `.ayy-toast--inline--busy` `.ayy-toast--inline--error` `.ayy-toast__icon` `.ayy-toast__content` `.ayy-toast__title` `.ayy-toast__description` `.ayy-toast__actions` `.ayy-toast__copy` `.ayy-toast__close` `.ayy-toast__backdrop` `.ayy-toast__image` `.ayy-toast__thumb` `.ayy-toast__media` `.ayy-toast__scrim` `.ayy-toast__center` `.ayy-toast__corner` `.ayy-toast__corner--top` `.ayy-toast__corner--top-start` `.ayy-toast__corner--bottom-start` `.ayy-toast__corner--bottom-end` `.ayy-toast__action` `.ayy-toast__status` `.ayy-toast__status--success` `.ayy-toast__status--busy` `.ayy-toast__status--error`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, error, leaving
- JS: toast(message, { description?, variant?, duration?, action?: { label, onClick }, copyable?, copyText?, id? }) → { id, dismiss }; toast.success/warning/error/info/long(message, options); toast.card(options) → { id, dismiss, status }; toast.copy(text, options); cardToast(options); inlineToastClass({ tone?, className? }); toast.dismiss(id?); configureToaster({ position?, label?, closeLabel?, clearLabel? }); toastClass({ variant?, className? })
- A11y: The region is aria-live="polite"; destructive toasts use role="alert". Timers pause while the toaster stack or a toast is hovered or focused, so there's time to read it and reach its action. Messages are set with textContent — never HTML.

## Progress (Feedback)
Thin progress bar. Determinate (--ayy-value 0–100) or indeterminate.
- Classes: `.ayy-progress` `.ayy-progress__bar` `.ayy-progress--sm` `.ayy-progress--lg` `.ayy-progress--success` `.ayy-progress--warning` `.ayy-progress--destructive` `.ayy-progress--ai` `.ayy-progress--indeterminate`
- States: error, loading
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: progressClass({ variant?, tone?, size?, indeterminate?, className? }) → string (tone is a deprecated alias of variant)
- A11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them). Give it an accessible name: aria-label or aria-labelledby.

## Progress ring (Feedback)
Progress as a ring that fills clockwise from the top: a focus timer, a daily goal, a habit's week, a small upload next to a file name. Determinate (--ayy-value 0–100) or indeterminate, with an optional value, time or icon in the middle.
- Classes: `.ayy-progress-ring` `.ayy-progress-ring__svg` `.ayy-progress-ring__track` `.ayy-progress-ring__bar` `.ayy-progress-ring__label` `.ayy-progress-ring--sm` `.ayy-progress-ring--lg` `.ayy-progress-ring--xl` `.ayy-progress-ring--success` `.ayy-progress-ring--warning` `.ayy-progress-ring--destructive` `.ayy-progress-ring--ai` `.ayy-progress-ring--indeterminate`
- States: error, loading, empty
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg` `xl`
- JS: progressRingClass({ variant?, size?, indeterminate?, className? }) → string; progressRingSvg (the SVG markup to put first inside the ring); progressRingSizes. The fill colour can be overridden with --ayy-progress-color, as on Progress.
- A11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them). Give it a name with aria-label or aria-labelledby. What the label in the middle says isn't read (a progressbar's content is presentational): put it in the name too ("Habit: 3 of 5 days this week"). The fill is drawn with the system highlight in High Contrast, the track in GrayText.

## Spinner (Feedback)
An indeterminate loading ring in the text colour, sized like an icon. For short waits on a small area or inside a button; Skeleton covers content that's loading.
- Classes: `.ayy-spinner` `.ayy-spinner--sm` `.ayy-spinner--lg`
- States: loading
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: spinnerClass({ size?, className? }) → string. Buttons: add aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: <Button loading>).
- A11y: A spinner on its own is a role="status" with an aria-label that says what's loading ("Loading invoices"). Inside a button, hide it (aria-hidden) and set aria-busy="true" on the button; the button's text still names it. Mark the region that's refreshing with aria-busy="true" until the new content is in. Under reduced motion it stops as a still ring; the label and aria-busy still say it's working.

## Skeleton (Feedback)
Placeholder shapes shown while content loads, with a subtle shimmer.
- Classes: `.ayy-skeleton` `.ayy-skeleton--text` `.ayy-skeleton--circle`
- States: loading
- JS: skeletonClass({ shape?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Skeletons are aria-hidden. Put aria-busy="true" on the container while loading, and remove it when content arrives. To name the loading region, give it role="status" and an aria-label — aria-label on a plain div is ignored. The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Empty state (Feedback)
What a list, table or page shows when there's nothing in it yet, or nothing matches: an optional icon tile, a title, one sentence on why, and the action that fills it.
- Classes: `.ayy-empty-state` `.ayy-empty-state--bordered` `.ayy-empty-state--compact` `.ayy-empty-state__title` `.ayy-empty-state__description` `.ayy-empty-state__actions`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: emptyStateClass({ bordered?, compact?, className? }) → string; emptyStateTitleClass, emptyStateDescriptionClass, emptyStateActionsClass constants.
- A11y: The title is a real heading at the level that fits the page (h2 under the page's h1, h3 inside a card). The icon tile is decorative: the title carries the meaning. When results change because of a search or filter, put the empty state inside a role="status" region (or announce the count) so screen reader users hear that nothing matched.

## Badge (Data display)
Small pill label for status, category or count. Optional pulsing status dot.
- Classes: `.ayy-badge` `.ayy-badge--muted` `.ayy-badge--outline` `.ayy-badge--success` `.ayy-badge--warning` `.ayy-badge--destructive` `.ayy-badge--info` `.ayy-badge--ai` `.ayy-badge__dot` `.ayy-badge__dot--static`
- States: error
- JS: badgeClass({ variant?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Colour is never the only signal — the label text must say the status. The dot is aria-hidden; it's decorative.

## Status dot (Data display)
A compact standalone status indicator dot for online presence, live event streaming, server health, and table row statuses.
- Classes: `.ayy-status-dot` `.ayy-status-dot--sm` `.ayy-status-dot--lg` `.ayy-status-dot--neutral` `.ayy-status-dot--success` `.ayy-status-dot--warning` `.ayy-status-dot--destructive` `.ayy-status-dot--info` `.ayy-status-dot--pulse`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: statusDotClass({ variant?, size?, pulse?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Colour is never the only signal — accompany standalone status dots with a text label or pass the label prop so screen readers announce it. When label is provided, sets role="status" and aria-label; when omitted, aria-hidden="true" treats the dot as decorative.

## Keyboard hint (Data display)
A keyboard key or shortcut hint drawn as a small keycap: in help text, menus, tooltips and search fields, with platform-specific modifier adaptation (macOS ⌘/⌥, Windows Ctrl/Win, Linux Super) and international layout awareness.
- Classes: `.ayy-kbd`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: kbdClass and keyboardHintClass constants. platformKeyLabel(key, platform) maps modifier names to platform symbols/names ("mod" → ⌘ on Mac, Ctrl on Windows/Linux; "meta" → ⌘ on Mac, Win on Windows, Super on Linux); platformKeyName(key, platform) gives its spoken name ("Command" for ⌘).
- A11y: Use the <kbd> element: screen readers and search know it's a key. Write modifier names out where symbols may not read well ("Ctrl" rather than "^"), or add aria-label="Command K" to a <kbd>⌘K</kbd> (screen readers pronounce "⌘" as "place of interest sign"). A shortcut hint doesn't replace aria-keyshortcuts on the control it triggers.

## Text highlight (Data display)
An inline text highlight for search matches or callout phrases. Subtle gray wash with clean underline by default, with warning (yellow), destructive (red), success (green), info (blue), and orange variants.
- Classes: `.ayy-text-highlight` `.ayy-text-highlight--warning` `.ayy-text-highlight--destructive` `.ayy-text-highlight--success` `.ayy-text-highlight--info` `.ayy-text-highlight--orange`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: textHighlightClass({ variant?, className? }) → string; textHighlightParts(text, query) splits text into matching and non-matching segments.
- A11y: Uses the standard <mark> HTML tag for search and text highlights, recognised by assistive technology. Maintains readable contrast across light, dark, and high-contrast themes via color-mix() and light-dark(). Under Windows High Contrast mode (forced-colors), highlights switch to the system Highlight and HighlightText colours.

## Avatar (Data display)
Round (or square) picture of a person or workspace, with initials that show when there's no image or it fails to load.
- Classes: `.ayy-avatar` `.ayy-avatar--sm` `.ayy-avatar--lg` `.ayy-avatar--xl` `.ayy-avatar--square` `.ayy-avatar__fallback` `.ayy-avatar__image` `.ayy-avatar-group`
- States: error
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg` `xl`
- JS: avatarClass({ size?, shape?, className? }); avatarInitials(name); avatarGroupClass, avatarImageClass, avatarFallbackClass constants
- A11y: The name goes on the root (aria-label); the <img> has alt="" and the initials are aria-hidden, so it's announced once. Give an AvatarGroup an aria-label like "5 collaborators". A failed image is hidden by React or @danitesler/ayywi/elements so the initials show. With CSS alone it renders as a plain disc.

## Icon (Data display)
Inline SVG icon from Hugeicons, ayywi's icon library: 6,000+ free Stroke Rounded icons on a 24px grid. It takes the text colour and follows the text size unless you pick one.
- Classes: `.ayy-icon` `.ayy-icon--sm` `.ayy-icon--md` `.ayy-icon--lg` `.ayy-icon--xl` `.ayy-icon--directional`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `auto` `sm` `md` `lg` `xl`
- JS: iconSvg(icon, { size?, directional?, label?, strokeWidth?, className? }) → SVG markup for innerHTML, v-html, {@html} or server templates; iconClass({ size?, directional?, className? }); iconSizes; type IconData (Hugeicons' format). Icons come from `npm i @hugeicons/core-free-icons`: import { Search01Icon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons". Plain HTML: paste the SVG with class="ayy-icon".
- A11y: Icons are decorative by default (aria-hidden): the text next to them carries the meaning. When the icon is the only thing saying something (a status, a verified mark), give it a label: <Icon label="Deployed">, or role="img" + aria-label on the <svg>. Icon-only buttons: aria-label goes on the button, the icon stays decorative. Strokes use currentColor, so icons follow the theme and Windows High Contrast colours with no extra CSS.

## Icon tile (Data display)
An app-icon squircle lit from below by the content's accent, with an SVG glyph in that accent. For products, plugins and services.
- Classes: `.ayy-icon-tile` `.ayy-icon-tile--sm` `.ayy-icon-tile--lg`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: iconTileClass({ size?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Usually decorative next to the product's name: aria-hidden="true" (React does this unless you pass aria-label). Standing alone, give it role="img" and an aria-label.

## Stat (Data display)
A headline number in the heading font, with a muted unit beside it and a short label: downloads, views, results.
- Classes: `.ayy-stat` `.ayy-stat--sm` `.ayy-stat__value` `.ayy-stat__unit` `.ayy-stat__label`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `md` `sm`
- JS: statClass({ size?, className? }) → string; statValueClass, statUnitClass, statLabelClass constants.
- A11y: Write abbreviations the way they should be read, or add the full number: <span aria-hidden="true">200k</span><span class="ayy-sr-only">200,000</span>. Keep the unit as text, not only an icon.

## List (Data display)
Rows of people, records, threads or settings: leading media (avatar, icon, icon tile), a title over a description, and trailing meta or a control. A link in the title makes the whole row clickable.
- Classes: `.ayy-list` `.ayy-list--divided` `.ayy-list--compact` `.ayy-list__item` `.ayy-list__content` `.ayy-list__title` `.ayy-list__description` `.ayy-list__meta` `.ayy-list__link`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- JS: listClass({ divided?, compact?, className? }) → string; listItemClass, listContentClass, listTitleClass, listDescriptionClass, listMetaClass, listLinkClass constants.
- A11y: It's a real list: screen readers announce how many rows there are. One link per row, in the title, so a row is one tab stop with a meaningful name. Buttons and switches in the row are separate tab stops after it. Mark the open row with aria-current="page" (it's a page) or "true" (a selection in a list-detail view); it gets a tint and a heavier title, not just colour. A switch or checkbox in a settings row needs its label: make the title a <label for> pointing at it. Avatars and icons in the leading slot are decorative when the title names the row.

## Property list (Data display)
A record's attributes as a definition list: a muted term (an icon and a label) and its value, side by side, wrapping under each other when the value doesn't fit.
- Classes: `.ayy-property-list` `.ayy-property-list--compact` `.ayy-property-list__row` `.ayy-property-list__term` `.ayy-property-list__label` `.ayy-property-list__icon` `.ayy-property-list__value` `.ayy-property-list__empty`
- States: empty
- JS: propertyListClass({ compact?, className? }) → string; propertyListRowClass, propertyListTermClass, propertyListLabelClass, propertyListIconClass, propertyListValueClass, propertyListEmptyClass constants.
- A11y: It's a real <dl>: screen readers announce a definition list and pair each term with its value. Each row is a <div> inside the <dl> (valid HTML) with exactly one <dt> and one <dd>, so the rows can wrap and flex. Icons in the term are decorative; the label names the row. An empty value says "Not set" in text, not a dash or a blank cell. A value edited in place keeps the nested InlineEdit's own label ("Change the version"); the term names the attribute, the control names the action.

## Swipe actions (Data display)
A list row that slides sideways to show buttons underneath, as in phone mail and task apps: swipe toward the end for Done, toward the start for Snooze or Delete. Works with touch, pen and mouse, follows the reading direction, and keyboards reach the buttons with Tab.
- Classes: `.ayy-swipe` `.ayy-swipe__content` `.ayy-swipe__actions` `.ayy-swipe__actions--start` `.ayy-swipe__actions--end` `.ayy-swipe__action` `.ayy-swipe__action--primary` `.ayy-swipe__action--success` `.ayy-swipe__action--warning` `.ayy-swipe__action--info` `.ayy-swipe__action--destructive`
- States: focus, open, dragging
- Element: `<ayy-swipe>`, events `ayy-open-change`
- JS: connectSwipe(row, { onOpenChange? }) → { open(side), close(), destroy() } wires the gesture on plain markup: drag past half a tray to keep it open; a tap on the row, a tap elsewhere, Esc or an action closes it. swipeActionClass({ variant?, className? }); swipeActionVariants; swipeClass, swipeContentClass, swipeActionsClass constants.
- A11y: Swiping is a shortcut, never the only way: offer the same actions in the row's page or a Menu, since many people can't or don't swipe. The actions are real buttons after the content in the tab order; a tray with focus shows over the row, and Esc closes an open row. Labels stay visible under the icons, so the tint isn't the only cue. Undo destructive actions (a Toast with Undo) rather than asking for confirmation in the middle of a gesture.

## Timeline (Data display)
Chronological list of events, milestones, or history with vertical connecting tracks, status markers, timestamps, and descriptions.
- Classes: `.ayy-timeline` `.ayy-timeline--alternate` `.ayy-timeline__item` `.ayy-timeline__track` `.ayy-timeline__marker` `.ayy-timeline__marker--pulse` `.ayy-timeline__content` `.ayy-timeline__time` `.ayy-timeline__title` `.ayy-timeline__body`
- States: pulse
- JS: timelineClass({ alternate?, className? }) → string; timelineMarkerClass({ pulse?, className? }) → string; timelineItemClass, timelineTrackClass, timelineContentClass, timelineTimeClass, timelineTitleClass, timelineBodyClass constants.
- A11y: Rendered as an ordered list (<ol>) by default so screen readers announce the item count and sequence. Timestamps use the semantic <time> element with tabular numbers for consistent alignment and screen reader comprehension. Decorative markers and track lines are marked aria-hidden="true" to prevent screen reader noise; important status information should be in the title or body. Active pulse rings are visual enhancements; screen readers receive the active status via text in the title, body, or an accessible badge. Supports Windows High Contrast mode via @media (forced-colors: active) with system CanvasText, Canvas, and Highlight colors.

## Frame (Data display)
A browser window around a screenshot, video or coded mock-up: a bar with three dots and an optional address, and a long soft shadow.
- Classes: `.ayy-frame` `.ayy-frame__bar` `.ayy-frame__title` `.ayy-frame__body`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: frameClass, frameBarClass, frameTitleClass, frameBodyClass constants.
- A11y: The screenshot is the content: give the <img> alt text that says what it shows, or wrap the frame in a <figure> with a <figcaption>. The dots are decoration (a pseudo-element).

## Chat (Data display)
A conversation: incoming bubbles at the start edge, the reader's own inverted at the end, a typing indicator and quick-reply buttons.
- Classes: `.ayy-chat` `.ayy-chat__message` `.ayy-chat__message--out` `.ayy-chat__bubble` `.ayy-chat__typing` `.ayy-chat__replies`
- States: loading
- JS: chatMessageClass({ direction?, className? }) → string; chatClass, chatBubbleClass, chatTypingClass, chatRepliesClass constants.
- A11y: Use role="log" on the conversation when messages arrive while the reader watches; they're announced politely, in order. The typing dots are an image with a name ("Dani is typing"); remove the element when the message lands. Quick replies are real buttons; after one is chosen, move focus to the next sensible place, not back to the top.

## Code block (Data display)
Formatted code container with header, filename, copy button, line numbers, and token styling for syntax highlighting.
- Classes: `.ayy-code-block` `.ayy-code-block--numbered` `.ayy-code-block__header` `.ayy-code-block__filename` `.ayy-code-block__actions` `.ayy-code-block__selector` `.ayy-code-block__chevron` `.ayy-code-block__menu` `.ayy-code-block__copy` `.ayy-code-block__pre` `.ayy-code-block__code` `.ayy-code-block__line` `.ayy-token-keyword` `.ayy-token-string` `.ayy-token-comment` `.ayy-token-function` `.ayy-token-number` `.ayy-token-operator` `.ayy-token-tag` `.ayy-token-attribute` `.ayy-token-property` `.ayy-token-punctuation` `.ayy-token-boolean`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, copied
- JS: codeBlockClass({ numbered?, className? }) → string; codeBlockHeaderClass({ className? }); codeBlockFilenameClass({ className? }); codeBlockActionsClass({ className? }); codeBlockSelectorClass({ className? }); codeBlockChevronClass({ className? }); codeBlockMenuClass({ className? }); codeBlockCopyClass({ className? }); codeBlockPreClass({ className? }); codeBlockCodeClass({ className? }); highlightCode(code, language?) → string; tokenizeCode(code, language?) → CodeToken[]; copyCodeBlock(button, { code?, timeout?, label?, copiedLabel? }) copies the code and shows the copied state; syncCodeBlockSelector(selectOrLang, codeBlock?) switches a code block to the chosen language: its label, and the code (and file name) from the block's own <template data-language="…" data-filename="…"> for that language, else the code stays; SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES, LANGUAGE_SNIPPETS; codeBlockCopyIcon, codeBlockCheckIcon (SVG markup).
- A11y: Pre element is scrollable via keyboard by adding tabindex="0". Copy button has an accessible label (aria-label) and announces state changes. Line numbers use CSS counters with user-select: none to avoid being copied into the clipboard. Syntax token classes maintain WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast against the surface background in light and dark themes.

## Table (Data display)
Data table with quiet hairlines, uppercase headers, hover rows, inline row actions and multi-select. Styles plain table elements under .ayy-table.
- Classes: `.ayy-table-wrap` `.ayy-table` `.ayy-table--compact` `.ayy-table__num` `.ayy-table__sort` `.ayy-table__select` `.ayy-table__actions` `.ayy-table__row-actions` `.ayy-table__row-actions--reveal`
- States: hover, focus, selected, sorted
- Element: `<ayy-table>`, events `ayy-sort`, `ayy-selection-change`
- JS: tableClass({ compact?, className? }); tableRowActionsClass({ reveal?, className? }); tableWrapClass, tableNumClass, tableSortClass, tableSelectClass, tableActionsClass constants; nextSortDirection(current) → "ascending" | "descending"; compareValues(a, b, direction?) sorts numbers (also "$1,240", "12 GB") by value and text with digits read as numbers, empty values last either way; connectTable(table, { onSort?, onSelectionChange? }) wires sort buttons and row checkboxes on plain markup (used by <ayy-table>).
- A11y: Use real <th> header cells with scope (React sets scope="col"). A <caption> or aria-label names the table for screen readers. Sorting is a button inside the header, so it's reachable by Tab and announced with the column's aria-sort. Only the sorted column carries aria-sort. Every row checkbox needs an aria-label naming its row ("Select INV-1042"); the select-all box is indeterminate when some rows are selected. Row action icon buttons and ⋯ menu triggers need an aria-label that names the row ("Edit Northwind", "More actions for Northwind").

## Grid (Data display)
Multi-select card grid for media assets, project cards, social media posts, screenshots and user records. Pairs card selection checkboxes, inline and ⋯ secondary item actions, a select-all toolbar and the floating bottom Action bar.
- Classes: `.ayy-grid-wrap` `.ayy-grid__toolbar` `.ayy-grid__select-all` `.ayy-grid` `.ayy-grid--compact` `.ayy-grid__item` `.ayy-grid__media` `.ayy-grid__header` `.ayy-grid__select` `.ayy-grid__actions` `.ayy-grid__actions--reveal` `.ayy-grid__title` `.ayy-grid__description` `.ayy-grid__body` `.ayy-grid__footer`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- Element: `<ayy-grid>`, events `ayy-selection-change`
- JS: gridClass({ compact?, className? }) → string; gridItemActionsClass({ reveal?, className? }) → string; gridWrapClass, gridToolbarClass, gridSelectAllClass, gridItemClass, gridMediaClass, gridHeaderClass, gridSelectClass, gridActionsClass, gridTitleClass, gridDescriptionClass, gridBodyClass, gridFooterClass constants; connectGrid(root, { onSelectionChange? }) wires select-all, card checkboxes, card-body click selection and Shift+click range selection (used by <ayy-grid>).
- A11y: Each selectable card contains a native Checkbox in GridItemSelect with an aria-label naming the item ("Select Hero screenshot"). Selected cards carry aria-selected="true" and a 2px border (Highlight outline in High Contrast mode), never colour alone. Per-card icon buttons and ⋯ DropdownMenu triggers carry an aria-label naming the item ("More actions for Hero screenshot"). GridItemActions with reveal uses opacity so controls remain in the Tab order and become visible on :focus-within.

## Chart (Data display)
Charts drawn by CSS with no library: columns and bars (grouped, stacked, 100%, horizontal, with lines over them), histograms, waterfalls, lines and areas (stacked, stepped), scatters and bubbles, donuts, pies, gauges, radars, heatmaps, funnels, a ranked bar list and sparklines. Bars, slices, cells and ticks take --ayy-value (0–100), dots --ayy-x/--ayy-y, lines are SVG paths from chartPath(). Series colours are the chart tokens in order, so a chart library can match them.
- Classes: `.ayy-chart` `.ayy-chart--stacked` `.ayy-chart--values` `.ayy-chart--horizontal` `.ayy-chart--histogram` `.ayy-chart--combo` `.ayy-chart--waterfall` `.ayy-chart--pie` `.ayy-chart--gauge` `.ayy-chart--radar` `.ayy-chart__plot` `.ayy-chart__tick` `.ayy-chart__bars` `.ayy-chart__column` `.ayy-chart__bar` `.ayy-chart__bar--up` `.ayy-chart__bar--down` `.ayy-chart__svg` `.ayy-chart__series` `.ayy-chart__series--compare` `.ayy-chart__line` `.ayy-chart__area` `.ayy-chart__gradient` `.ayy-chart__labels` `.ayy-chart__axis` `.ayy-chart__dot` `.ayy-chart__ring` `.ayy-chart__track` `.ayy-chart__slice` `.ayy-chart__total` `.ayy-chart__total-value` `.ayy-chart__grid` `.ayy-chart__label` `.ayy-chart__legend` `.ayy-chart__legend-item` `.ayy-chart__legend-item--compare` `.ayy-chart__legend-item--line` `.ayy-chart__swatch` `.ayy-chart__legend-value` `.ayy-bar-list` `.ayy-bar-list__item` `.ayy-bar-list__label` `.ayy-bar-list__value` `.ayy-sparkline` `.ayy-heatmap` `.ayy-heatmap__row` `.ayy-heatmap__label` `.ayy-heatmap__cell` `.ayy-heatmap__key` `.ayy-funnel` `.ayy-funnel__step` `.ayy-funnel__label` `.ayy-funnel__bar` `.ayy-funnel__value` `.ayy-funnel__rate`
- States: hover
- JS: chartScale(values, { ticks?, min?, max? }) → { min, max, ticks } with a round top; chartPercent(value, max, min?) → 0–100 for --ayy-value; chartPath(values, { min?, max?, smooth?, step?, band?, base? }) → { line, area } path data for the 0 0 100 100 box (step: steps; band: points over column centres; base: the area's floor, for stacking); chartStack(series, { percent? }) → each series' running top; chartBins(values, { bins?, min?, max? }) → { edges, counts } for a histogram; chartSlices(values, { total? }) → [{ start, value }] shares for ring slices; chartRadar(values, { min?, max? }) → a closed path and chartRadarPoint(index, count, share?, radius?) → { x, y } for spokes and labels; chartWaterfall(steps) → [{ from, to, change }]; chartColors(target?, count?) → resolved rgb() strings and chartTheme(target?) → { colors, text, muted, grid, surface, fontFamily } for canvas libraries (Chart.js, ECharts); chartClass({ stacked?, values?, horizontal?, type?, className? }) with type one of chartTypes (histogram, combo, waterfall, pie, gauge, radar), chartSeriesClass({ compare?, className? }), chartLegendItemClass({ compare?, line?, className? }) and part class constants.
- A11y: The drawing is aria-hidden. The numbers go in a table with a <caption> saying what the chart shows, inside a <div class="ayy-sr-only"> (as React renders it): a table can't be narrower than its content, so hiding the table itself lets a long caption widen the page. Add a visible Table if people need to compare values. Don't rely on colour alone: a legend names the series in the same order, the comparison series is dashed, and a title or a Stat states the takeaway ("Up 12% on last week"). Series tokens keep 3:1 against every surface in every theme. In High Contrast bars and lines take system colours, alternating between CanvasText and Highlight. A Sparkline with a label is an image with that name; give it the trend in words ("Revenue, last 14 days, up 12%"). A gauge is one value, so it's a meter: role="meter" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, an aria-valuetext in words ("$7.2K of $10K") and a name. A funnel and a bar list are text already and need no table. Waterfall changes are signed (+$6.4K, −$1.3K) as well as coloured, and a donut's legend gives each share as a number.
